scenes.narration: Welcome to What is Rabies, part of the Canine Rabies course.

Rabies is a viral disease that attacks the central nervous system. It is almost always fatal once clinical signs appear. It is transmitted through the saliva of an infected animal, usually via a bite. It is preventable with timely vaccination.

payload.heading: Key facts
bullets: Viral disease attacking the central nervous system
Almost always fatal once clinical signs appear
Transmitted through saliva, usually via a bite

scenes.narration: The World Health Organization rates post-exposure prophylaxis administered promptly after a bite as highly effective at preventing disease onset.

payload.claim: Prompt post-exposure prophylaxis prevents disease onset after a bite.

scenes.narration: That's the essentials of rabies. Continue to the next lesson for the vaccination protocol.
